bug_semantics: The experimental --http-api Express server binds to 127.0.0.1 with no authentication. After action arguments were added, POST /api/action/:action forwards the JSON body into app actions including openFiles. A browser page that becomes same-origin with the API via DNS rebinding (or CSRF before Origin is rejected) can POST attacker-controlled paths such as UNC shares. Electron/OS then fetches those paths, producing SSRF and Windows NTLM hash leakage. Commit 260802348955231442c4bae6c2d9d8ede947af0a hardens the server by requiring a localhost Host and rejecting any Origin.
flaw_origin: Commit 533074ddaec808b4f9c383b9e5774624abc2a524 is the smallest first-write of the reported CWE-918 path: it changed POST /api/shortcuts/:action (action name only) into POST /api/action/:action that calls onKeyboardAction(action, [req.body]) and registered HTTP openFiles against openFilesActionArgsSchema (string paths). Direct parent e5f23510e1bb8933f14ffd08833e987a0eb6bc61 still has the localhost HTTP server but cannot pass paths. Earlier a3cbce61901651d526d9575f3c4bb2aafc21c40f only created the unauthenticated name-only API; f67761903935d35fd85609cfb5c6f016a8f431c6 later moved public/httpServer.js to src/main/httpServer.ts. The BIC is a direct one-parent change, not a move, refactor, revert, backport, release, or squash.
